submission.justification: Radiator-R2 at 3 cm thickness delivers the highest pion/kaon separation (4.4-4.6σ at 10 GeV/c) among the candidate options, as established by both recent and earlier simulations. It satisfies the requirement for maximizing particle identification, and its performance at this thickness outperforms both thinner and thicker versions, as well as the other radiators. All project constraints are satisfied and no lifetime/performance risks are indicated in the available documentation.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 is listed as a candidate in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must keep its performance over the experiment's lifetime.
requirements.evidence: No documentation indicates degradation for R2; performance is stable in simulations and previous studies.
3 cm thickness is within the allowed range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: Simulations show R2 at 3 cm gives 4.4-4.6 sigma separation, the highest among all options.
